operations.old_text: The validator is one semantic checker with independent proof adapters, not a copy of either census loop. It must derive status from predicates rather than trust producer labels. Checks include schema/bytes, provenance and hashes, cutoff replay, conjugacy, root evidence, inversion, reciprocity, repetition, uniqueness, termination, coverage, and zero unresolved records. Failure yields rejection, bounded-incomplete, or not-evaluable status under a later state table.
operations.new_text: The independent-validator contract remains prospective. Its trust graph has producer nodes BP and CP, adapter nodes \(A_{\mathrm{BP}}\) and \(A_{\mathrm{CP}}\), a byte parser \(V_{\mathrm{parse}}\), predicate kernels \(V_{\mathrm{pred}}\), a fixture-oracle node \(O\), theorem-encoding records, external libraries, and accountable implementers. In any future implementation, the intended trusted computing base would be limited to the then-frozen schema and proof-type registry, canonical-byte and digest rules, \(V_{\mathrm{parse}}\), \(V_{\mathrm{pred}}\), and explicitly disclosed theorem encodings; producer status labels and search code would remain outside it. Sharing the schema, digest specification, or a disclosed general-purpose arithmetic or cryptographic library is allowed. Sharing a theorem encoding, adapter helper, or fixture-generation utility must be disclosed and prevents that component from being described as independently implemented. Reuse of producer decision code inside \(V_{\mathrm{pred}}\), a mutable or producer-derived expected-output oracle, an undisclosed dependency, or one hidden implementation serving as both producer and checker is disqualifying. Every future node must carry an accountable implementer, source-tree digest, build-environment digest, and build SHA-256. At present \texttt{BP}, \texttt{CP}, both adapters, the checker, and an independently authored oracle are \texttt{UNAVAILABLE\_COMPONENT\_NOT\_IMPLEMENTED}; consequently no build hash is invented and validator independence is not established. Failure at parsing, proof dispatch, cutoff replay, conjugacy, root, inversion, reciprocity, repetition, uniqueness, termination, coverage, or unresolved-record checks must yield rejected, bounded-incomplete, or not-evaluable status rather than acceptance.

operations.old_text: The schema has explicit incompatibility rules. A complete run cannot contain an unresolved conjugacy, root, cutoff, or owner disposition. A primitive record cannot simultaneously report an exponent greater than one. A repetition cannot create an owner ID distinct from its primitive root's owner. A self-reciprocal flag requires its own conjugacy-to-inverse evidence, while external inverse pairing is required regardless of that flag. A complete status is incompatible with a failed termination or coverage predicate, a missing correction binding, duplicate canonical owner IDs, hash drift, or an unrecognized proof type.
operations.new_text: The paper-level common contract is \path{P33-OWNER-CERT/1} with proof registry \path{P33-PROOF-TYPES/1}. Its closed allowed top-level field set is \path{schema_version}, \path{proof_registry_digest}, \path{surface_id}, \path{producer_id}, \path{run_id}, \path{record_type}, \path{candidate_id}, \path{producer_representation}, \path{enumeration_provenance}, \path{oriented_class_digest}, \path{primitive_root_digest}, \path{root_exponent}, \path{inverse_class_digest}, \path{owner_id}, \path{owner_member_digests}, \path{cutoff}, \path{cutoff_disposition}, \path{proof_type}, \path{proof_payload}, \path{input_digest}, \path{theorem_version_digest}, \path{implementation_digest}, \path{correction_provenance_digest}, \path{clock_id}, \path{subtype_id}, \path{owner_rule_id}, \path{termination_witness}, \path{coverage_digest}, \path{unresolved_count}, \path{validator_version}, \path{validator_digest}, \path{fixture_set_digest}, \path{predicate_decisions}, \path{rejected_incompatibilities}, and \path{state}. The record family determines the mandatory subset described in the preceding schema table; unlisted fields, missing mandatory fields, or unrecognized enum values fail closed. The closed \path{record_type} enum is \path{run_header}, \path{candidate}, \path{conjugacy}, \path{root}, \path{inversion}, \path{owner}, \path{repetition}, \path{termination}, \path{coverage}, or \path{validation}; \path{surface_id} is \path{BOLZA-SOURCE-LOCK} or \path{NAZARENKO-EXP-OCTAGON-G2}. The closed \path{state} enum is \path{declared}, \path{parsed}, \path{predicate_checked}, \path{accepted}, \path{rejected}, \path{bounded_incomplete}, or \path{not_evaluable}. The proof registry admits only \path{exact_conjugator}, \path{canonical_conjugacy_normal_form}, \path{maximal_root}, \path{no_proper_power}, \path{systolic_primitive}, \path{exact_cutoff_comparison}, \path{exact_trace_comparison}, \path{conjugacy_to_inverse}, \path{termination_measure}, and \path{coverage_replay}; each payload must name its input digests and supply the exact witness consumed by the correspondingly named predicate. State moves are \path{declared} to \path{parsed} to \path{predicate_checked} and then to exactly one terminal state; only the checker may derive the final move. A complete run is rejected if any conjugacy, root, cutoff, inverse, owner, termination, or coverage disposition is unresolved; if a proof type cannot be dispatched, the run is \path{not_evaluable}. A primitive record cannot have exponent greater than one, a repetition cannot mint an owner distinct from its primitive root's owner, and a self-reciprocal record requires separate conjugacy-to-inverse evidence plus its external inverse link. Failed termination or coverage, a missing correction binding, duplicate canonical owner IDs, digest drift, or an unrecognized proof type precludes acceptance. This closes the semantic contract at manuscript level but does not assert that a producer, schema file, proof registry file, adapter, fixture, or validator has been implemented or run.

BP's bounded domain is empty only after exact replay of \(\operatorname{sys}(S_{\mathrm{Bolza}})>21/10\); failure or digest drift stops as \texttt{UPSTREAM\_REPLAY\_CONTRADICTION}. CP's bounded domain is the exact identity-connected centre-guard component from the frozen certificate \path{papers/28-bolza-magnetic-flow/results/round8_control_finite_ball_certificate.json}, SHA-256 \url{c1bf68a8a1485665680dba01d0012fb691c7ca1a795e36334639e34bbbdbcb1f}. Its order is FIFO breadth-first traversal from the identity through \(g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3,g_0^{-1},g_1^{-1},g_2^{-1},g_3^{-1}\), with exact normalized-state deduplication; each neighbour is classified by the exact centre guard \(\lvert\alpha\rvert^2\leq20000\), and final streams are lexicographically sorted by canonical state bytes. Cutoff admission is always the exact comparison \(\ell(g)\leq21/10\), never a rounded decimal. BP terminates on a verified strict systole replay; CP terminates only when the FIFO queue is empty and every outgoing edge from every included state has an included or rejected disposition. Coverage binds the sorted included and rejected streams, theorem and input digests, cutoff, and a complete unresolved ledger; the accepted upstream stream digests are \url{814f72badce2cc90e8e26edc2a7db18d52c4c334c0f5dfc5bf7d8e4a90dcf545} and \url{3017c21285daad5a1173b076c9b5700975f67cdbbdaa8a6218e80d4bc89da6f4}. An independent checker must reconstruct the bound and both stream digests; nonzero unresolved count yields bounded-incomplete or not-evaluable status. These artifacts fix input bytes but do not discharge the future obligations to bind exact theorem and algorithm versions, prove applicability, and emit checkable proof payloads rather than status labels. This paragraph fixes an executable contract from accepted upstream bytes; it executes no producer, replay, owner quotient, or census here.

operations.old_text: Package B concerns the meanings carried across that producer boundary. A common record must say which surface, run, candidate, oriented class, primitive root, inverse partner, and owner it concerns. It must also distinguish an assertion about a class from the payload offered to support that assertion. The schema cannot infer primitivity from a short word, infer ownership from equal length, or infer self-reciprocity from the external convention that pairs every class with its inverse. Repetitions must point back to the owner of their primitive root, while a self-reciprocal flag must carry separate conjugacy-to-inverse evidence. Likewise, a cutoff disposition must record the exact or proof-bearing comparison it uses rather than a rounded decimal. These are semantic constraints on any future serialization; the present manuscript neither fixes the bytes nor selects a universal proof language.
operations.new_text:
Package B fixes owner semantics across the producer boundary. Let \(d(g)\) be the canonical digest of an oriented full-group conjugacy class after its conjugacy predicate has passed, and let \(d(g^{-1})\) be computed independently under the same rule. If a separate conjugacy-to-inverse proof passes, the self-reciprocal owner has the deduplicated singleton member list \([d(g)]\), cardinality one, and an inverse link to itself. Otherwise the owner has the two distinct member digests \([\min(d(g),d(g^{-1})),\max(d(g),d(g^{-1}))]\), cardinality two, in byte-lexicographic order, with reciprocal inverse links. The owner identifier is
\[
 \operatorname{SHA256}(\texttt{P33-owner-v1}\mathbin{\|\!\|}\texttt{surface-id}\mathbin{\|\!\|}\texttt{member-count}\mathbin{\|\!\|}\texttt{ordered-member-bytes}),
\]
where each separator and field encoding follows the canonical-byte contract. Duplicate candidate rows are removed before this derivation and cannot change the member list or identifier. A repetition records its primitive-root digest and the already derived root owner identifier; it never mints an owner. Equal length, trace, word, homology, or literal matrix data cannot set self-reciprocity or merge owners. These rules fix membership, deduplication, inverse links, and owner IDs without asserting that any owner has been computed.

Integers use unsigned or explicitly signed base-10 strings without leading zeros; a rational uses the canonical byte-order object \texttt{\{den,num\}}, where \texttt{den} is positive, \texttt{num} is signed, and the two integers are coprime; floating-point numbers, NaN, infinities, duplicate keys, and unknown fields are forbidden. The record digest is SHA-256 of the ASCII domain prefix \texttt{P33-OWNER-CERT}, one zero byte, the schema version, one zero byte, the proof-registry digest, one zero byte, and the canonical record bytes. Records are ordered by \texttt{surface\_id}, \texttt{record\_type}, and record digest; owner members use the deterministic rule stated below. Compatibility requires exact equality of both \texttt{schema\_version} and \texttt{proof\_registry\_digest}.
